security_concerns.summary: An accepted str subclass can override encode(), causing native pathname bytes to differ from the validated literal component and escape the retained destination parent.
security_concerns.reproduction: A RedirectedComponent(str) containing the literal string "final" overrides encode() to return b"../escaped". On the real Linux libc renameat2 call, the stage directory moves to the owned fixture root/escaped, not destination/final; the winning directory inode matches the original stage.
security_concerns.evidence: test_component_subclass.py::test_accepted_str_subclass_must_not_escape_literal_component; 1 failed in 0.37s, actual private-filesystem operation, not a synthetic native return.
security_concerns.threat_scope: Requires an in-process Python caller supplying a non-builtin str subtype. No plain built-in-str bypass, remote exploit, hostile namespace requirement bypass, or privilege escalation is claimed. The public annotation is str and the implementation explicitly accepts str subtypes; the exact-component guarantee nevertheless is not met for all accepted inputs.
security_concerns.recommendation: In a separate authorized fix/review cycle, reject string subclasses with an exact-type check, or bind validation and both source inspection/native use to non-overridable exact bytes. Add the independently failing regression; do not automatically fix in this review.
